<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `52b05f7903afc65297d89744b11dffd7e2f1769c` — the merge of head `f20d249baf18db795aaaf2edb6bb601da64539f9` into base `6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 52b05f7903afc65297d89744b11dffd7e2f1769c && git checkout 52b05f7903afc65297d89744b11dffd7e2f1769c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38 f20d249baf18db795aaaf2edb6bb601da64539f9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38 && git merge --no-ff f20d249baf18db795aaaf2edb6bb601da64539f9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Scope: .changeset/32607-two-enabled-row-holders.md, .changeset/32607-two-row-holders-semantic-entry.md, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.two-row-holders-bare-read-refused.ts, and the PR title and body + read as cited code, not reviewed: `readMetaItem` in packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, `packagelessAddress` and `packagelessContentPackage` in protocol-environment-rows.ts, `readItemActiveRows` in protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts, `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` in protocol.ts, `packageScopedHoldersOf`, `overlaySlotBinding`, `settledPairRowBinding`, `isBundleAddition`, `getPackageScopedItem` and `getEnvironmentScopedItem` in packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, `pairsOf` in packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts, content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx

Contract review and epic red-line read of card #32607, read at 2026-11-14T00:46Z. Inputs: the card and its rulings (6820653691, 6821134180, 6836791341), the diff of this head against merge base `89d7bef0`, the PR title and body, report 6868555489, the check-runs on this head, knock 6868544976. Claim 6868561553. Every finding below is by reading; nothing was run here.

### ① Derived judgments

- The declaration lines are present and of the right kind: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none`, the BREAKING banner, the `!` title, `adr-0087: registered` with the semantic entry. A read that served and now refuses is `narrowed`, as declared.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds by this seat's own reading. No skill and no docs page teaches the row saved first. The pages that speak of a name two packages hold (import-mappings.mdx, analytics.mdx, permission-sets.mdx) already teach the refusal naming each, so the read now agrees with them. The lifecycle page's bullet on a dependent's added locale teaches a base that ships, which the guard keeps.
- The FROM and TO table is right for the shape the pins cover: two enabled packages, one row each of one name at one member, no shipper, a type that is no bundle.
- Two "not moved" sentences do not hold as written, by reading: "pair rows make no holder" (M1) and "`/layers` keeps the package-less writes' refusal" together with the bundled-type row of the table (M2).

### ② Semver level

- Right: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `patch` on `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head at the time of reading: 64 runs, 26 success, 11 skipped, 27 in progress (Test Core 8 shards, Test UI 16 shards, three type checks), none failed. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green. The verdict below is FAIL, which does not wait for them.
- CI skipped the dogfood shards on this head (the gate job concluded in half a minute, its matrix skipped). The battery reading (462 files passed) is the report's.
- Order. Merge base `89d7bef0`; `main` is at `1169d64f`, twelve commits past it. None is on a path of this diff; #33149 and #33119 add other files beside the new semantic entry. A `git merge-tree` of `main` and this head reports no conflict.
- `Fixes #32607` closes a card whose sub-issue #32663 is open (the writer's registry keeps one bare slot per stored name). That card changes the registry holder set this judgment unions with the rows, so M1 and M2 read differently once it lands. The seat's to sequence.
- Residual left open by the declaration, no carrier named: a package-less row beside the rows of two packages returns the read "as it was" (`rows.unbound`), so the plain read still takes a row by store order while `/layers` refuses naming both. It is the card's own symptom on a neighbouring shape. The seat's to route.
- The row judgment's union and its pair filter also serve the arm #32354 landed for a disabled holder. M1's reading reaches that arm on `main` too; that part is not this diff's.

### ④ Design judgment

Red-line 1 read of the guard `abd91aad9e` (asked in the knock). It does not loosen resolution. The guard sits inside the arm this PR adds (no disabled holder), which `main` answered `undefined` without exception, and it returns that same `undefined`. It counts shippers as `packagelessContentPackage` counts them, at any member. No read `main` refused is served through it.

`servedRowHolderOf`, the new arm. The served set is the registry's holders of the name united with the packages the active rows are bound to at the member. With no shipper the registry knows a row-only name through one bare slot per member, the row written or hydrated last, while the rows name every package. The two sets are read at different grains (the name, and the member) and from different sources (one slot, and every row). The pinned shape is the one where that does not matter. M1 and M2 are two where it does.

The hand-over in both transports (`isItemOfDisabledPackage`) catches whatever the plain read throws and asks only whether step 1c has a refusal for the address. See S1.

The item face now reads the name's active rows once more on every read naming no package of a by-package type that no enabled package ships at the member and that has no environment item. See S2.

Findings:

- **M1 must-fix. A pair's row beside a row-held name is counted as a second holder in one save order.** Shape: package X stores a row of `d`, X's customization pair stores an undeclared row of `d`, no package ships `d`, nothing is disabled, any by-package type. When X's row is the bare slot's entry, the registry's holders are X, `pairsOf(X)` names the pair, the pair's row is filtered, one holder remains and the read is `main`'s. When the pair's row is the entry, `overlaySlotBinding` binds it to the pair itself (no composite holder for the pair to be a pair of), the registry's holders are the pair alone, `pairsOf` of a pair is empty, neither row is filtered, and the read is refused 409 naming X and its own pair. So the answer follows which row was saved last, and a pair is named as a holder, against the docblock's own rule and the changeset's "pair rows make no holder". Asked: a pin of this shape in both save orders, before and after a reboot, on the plain read, `/published` and the execution face, showing one answer and no refusal naming a pair; and the judgment made to agree with it. If the pin is green at this head as written, post the reading and M1 is withdrawn.
- **M2 must-fix. A dependent's added member over a row-held base is refused naming the base and the dependent, and `/layers` moves with it.** Shape: `email_template`; base A stores `en-US` of a name nobody ships; D, which declares A, stores `fr-FR`. The registry holds A alone (D is a bundle addition, #28802). The rows at `fr-FR` name D. The union is two, so the read at `fr-FR` naming no package is refused 409 naming A and D, where #28802 says an addition is no second holder of the name. On `main` that read served D's row (`packagelessContentPackage` with no shipper takes the row's own binding). `/layers` at `fr-FR` was not refused on `main` and is refused 409 here: the owner step's read throws, step 1c has no refusal for one candidate, and the error is rethrown. The guard closes this only for a base that ships in code. Asked: the same pin on the plain read, `/layers`, `/published` and the execution face at the added member, and the holders judged at one grain. I did not read the write gate: if it refuses D's row over a row-held base, post that refusal and M2 is withdrawn.
- **S1 should-fix. The hand-over does not look at what it caught.** For a name two packages ship in code, each with its own bound overlay row, the owner step's read throws the registry's refusal (as on `main`), step 1c has a refusal for two bound rows, and `/layers` now leads with the writes' sentence where it led with the plain read's. The A1 CONTROL pins two code holders with no rows, so it does not reach this. Either hand over only the refusal the row judgment made, or declare this row and pin it. The comment "every other refusal is rethrown" is true of neither.
- **S2 should-fix. One more store round trip on the hot path.** `host.readItemActiveRows(type, name)` in `servedRowHolderOf` is the uncached read; `readMetaItem` then reads the same rows through the overlay cache. Before this PR the row read was skipped unless some package was disabled. It now runs on every execution-face read of a Studio-authored flow, tool, skill or agent, and on every miss. Share the read with `readMetaItem`, or take it through the cache as that read does.
- **n1 nit.** No pin covers a bundled type or a member other than the canonical one; every new pin is a `dashboard`. M2's pin would be the first.

### ① Derived judgments

- The declaration stands: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none`, the BREAKING banner, the `!` title, `adr-0087: registered`. The interdiff moves no answer beyond the declared ones. It takes two shapes back out of the refusal (M1, M2) and one out of the hand-over (S1).
- The changeset's "Not moved" paragraph and the body's table now name those three shapes, and each sentence agrees with the code as read.
- The body's file count is ten, as the diff against the merge base is.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and right: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `patch` on `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 71 runs, 58 success, 13 skipped, none failed. Test Core is green on all eight shards, shard 4 included; the type checks, the lints, `Check Changeset` (both runs, the second started by the body edit) and the PR-body guards are green. The dogfood shards were skipped by CI again.
- The body reports that Test Core 4/8 was red on `5d3a6c75` (the one-read pins of #24371). That run was in progress when record 6868755969 was read; it is the same defect as that record's S2.
- Order. The merge base is still `89d7bef0`; `main` is at `7257f57a`, 24 commits past it. One is on a path of this diff: #33119 on `protocol.ts`, in other hunks. A `git merge-tree` of `main` and this head reports no conflict. #33166, landed since, judges a stored row under two code holders; the shipper guard keeps such a name out of this arm.
- The body's Carried section names the three things record 6868755969 left with the seat: the package-less row beside two packages' rows, the save-order pick between a package's row and its pair's undeclared row, and #32663. The seat's to route.
- The local runs (97 of 97 gates, the four suites, the dogfood battery, ablations 4 and 5, the red readings before the fix) are the report's; none was run here.

### ④ Design judgment

`storedRowHoldersRefusal` (M1, M2). Closed. The arm with no disabled holder now counts only the packages the item's active rows are bound to at the member, less the rows the reads decline and less a row whose package is a pair of another package the rows or the registry name. The registry's holders no longer enter the count; they only help recognise a pair. For M1's shape the base is always among the rows, so its pair's row is filtered in either order. For M2's shape the rows at `fr-FR` name the dependent alone. The pinned shape (two packages, one row each at one member) still counts two. The arm still only refuses or leaves the read as it was, so the red-line 1 read of record 6868755969 stands.

The hand-over (S1). Closed. The judgment marks its own refusal under a registered symbol and both transports hand over only a marked error. The refusal beside a disabled holder and the registry's refusal are not marked and are rethrown, as on `main`. The key is spelled in three files; the A1 pins on both transports fail if one drifts.

The one read (S2). Closed. The face reads the rows through the overlay cache and hands them to `readMetaItem`, which takes them only for the same type and name and otherwise reads as before. One consequence, judged acceptable: the judgment beside a disabled holder (#32354) now sees the rows the read sees, through the same cache, where it read the store afresh.

Red-line 2 read of the two residuals (asked in the knock). Neither is made or widened by this PR; both are `main`'s answers, left as they were and named in the changeset and in Carried.

- (a) A package-less row beside the rows of two packages. This one is a standing departure from red line 2: three rows, no one holder, and the plain read serves one by store order while `/layers` refuses. The registry already says such a row is "a customization of a name it cannot say whose" and binds it to no package; the read does not follow. It is the card's own symptom one shape over, so it owes a card before `Fixes #32607` closes the subject, and the answer (refuse naming both, or read past the package-less row) is a ruling, not a dev's pick. Not a must-fix here: the PR declares it unmoved and it is.
- (b) A package's row beside its pair's undeclared row. No second holder exists here, so nothing is guessed between packages: red line 2 in its strict reading is kept, and this PR now keeps the pair out of the refusal in both orders. What follows save order is which layer of one holder's stack is served, and by the report's measurement `/published` serves the package's row in both orders while the plain read does not. That is a determinism defect of the one holder's read, to be carried on its own card (it sits beside #32662, the pair address after a reboot). Not this PR's.

The pins. M1 runs both save orders before and after a reboot and asserts no refusal on the plain read, `/published` and the execution face. M2 runs both save orders before and after a reboot at `fr-FR` on the plain read, `/layers` and the execution face, with the base's `en-US` as its control. The S1 control lays a row under each of two code holders. Each is reported red before its fix.

Findings:

- **n1 of record 6868755969.** Closed: M2 is a pin on a bundled type at a member other than the canonical one.
- **n2 nit, new.** The M2 pin fixes today's answer for a row-held base: the read naming no package at the added member serves the dependent's row. For a base that ships, the same read answers 404 (#28802, and the lifecycle page teaches it). The pin is right about `main` and about this PR; whether a row-held base should answer as a shipped one does is a question for the seat, and this pin is where that change would meet it. No change asked.

M1, M2, S1 and S2 of record 6868755969 are closed on this head. No must-fix, no should-fix.

No tests were run here: measured with git only (`git diff`, `git merge-tree`), read the code at the merged head, relied on CI and the card thread's green runs.
Inputs: records 6870642184 (PASS) and 6868755969 (FAIL), the PR body as it stands, `compare/89d7bef033...67274acad6` (25 commits), the check-runs on this head, and main at `0b89b33978` when I read it.

### (1) The interdiff
